items.stem: A designer prompts an image tool and ships the result. In many jurisdictions, what is the most accurate statement about copyright in a purely AI-generated image?

options.text: Protection may be limited or unavailable where no human authorship is present
options.rationale: Correct: several jurisdictions require human authorship for copyright to subsist.

options.text: The image is automatically fully copyrighted to the prompter in every jurisdiction
options.rationale: Overstated: rules on AI authorship vary and often require human creative contribution.

options.text: The tool vendor always owns the copyright regardless of the terms
options.rationale: Ownership depends on the tool's terms, not an automatic vendor rule.

options.text: AI images are always in the public domain worldwide
options.rationale: There is no universal rule placing all AI output in the public domain.

items.explanation: Correct: several jurisdictions require human authorship for copyright to subsist.

items.stem: Which TWO practices most reduce copyright risk when a team uses generative AI for client work? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Keep records of prompts, sources and tool licences used
options.rationale: Correct: provenance records support licensing and defend against claims.

options.text: Review outputs for substantial similarity to known works
options.rationale: Correct: similarity review catches likely infringement before release.

options.text: Assume all generated output is original and skip review
Remove all human involvement to avoid liability
options.rationale: Removing human review increases, not decreases, risk.

items.explanation: Correct: provenance records support licensing and defend against claims.

items.stem: Why can the data used to train a generative model raise copyright questions?

options.text: Training data may include works still protected by third-party copyright
options.rationale: Correct: protected works in training data are the core of many disputes.

options.text: Training always destroys the original works
options.rationale: Training does not destroy sources; copies may persist.

options.text: Only data older than 100 years is ever used
options.rationale: Models commonly train on recent, in-copyright material.

options.text: Copyright never applies to anything on the internet
options.rationale: Material online is frequently still in copyright.

items.explanation: Correct: protected works in training data are the core of many disputes.
